body: Deep-dive-generated forward test (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Live deep dive #2 (first US live run), company drawn at random (method test, L9/L21). Probability 0.42 (naive base rate 0.45) that: KEX total price return from 20-Nov-2026 (close $122.89) to 30-Sep-2027 beats SPY (close $689.81 on 20-Nov-2026). Our reasoning: no edge on the cycle claimed; the worksheet DCF sits well below the price and insiders sold $22M with no buys, against ~4-5%/yr buybacks, a strong 2026 print (EPS +14%) and a power-gen backlog; the stock fell 16% from $146 (28-Oct) into a falling market, so part of the de-rating has happened. Naive base: share of US single stocks beating the S&P 500 over ~10 months is a little below half because returns are right-skewed [EST, unverified; Bessembinder context]. Resolution: YES if (KEX close on the last trading day on or before 30-Sep-2027 / 122.89) > (SPY close on the same day / 689.81); split-adjusted closes, dividends ignored (KEX pays none; SPY ~1.2%/yr is a small handicap stated here). Source: Yahoo v8 daily closes KEX and SPY (Nasdaq.com historical as check). Resolve by 2027-09-30; score with Brier vs the base rate to test whether deep-dive probabilities beat naive base rates.
